subject: Service guarantee modification request — order form & evidence pack
body:
--- Message 1 of 5 ---
From: Alice Reynolds <alice.reynolds@atlantichealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@atlantichealth.com
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Request: tailored SLA language & evidence for enterprise order form

Hi Lukas,

As we get ready to finalize the SOW and order form for the pilot, procurement is asking for a bespoke addendum to the SLA that: 1) clarifies cross-region failover latency expectations, 2) defines a degradations credit schedule for sustained partial outage, and 3) lists the telemetry evidence you can provide (retention, sample traces, incident runbooks).

I've attached our latest SOW (Atlantic_SOW_v2.pdf) and the procurement template for orderform redlines. Can you confirm what pieces of evidence Redwood will commit to deliver during the onboarding window, and whether we can get orderform wording that maps to the credit schedule procurement requires?

Thanks,
Alice Reynolds
Director, Procurement
Atlantic Health Systems

Attachment: Atlantic_SOW_v2.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: Procurement_Orderform_Template.docx (docx)

--- Message 2 of 5 ---
From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Reynolds <alice.reynolds@atlantichealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: tailored SLA language & evidence for enterprise order form

Hi Alice — thanks for sending. I looped in Marissa (sales ops/legal touch) and Karthik (service commitments/product) for the specifics. High level: we can provide a custom SLA addendum that enumerates: regional failover expectations, a three-tier credit schedule tied to availability band and mean latency, and an evidence pack that includes 30/90 day latency histograms, per-route error rates, sample incident postmortems, and a signed retention statement for telemetry.

Before Marissa drafts language, can you confirm: (a) procurement's required credit bands (they often ask for a 99.95 / 99.9 / 99.0 split), (b) any hard constraints on MTTR vs detection window, and (c) who on your legal team will review redlines?

If helpful, we can propose order form phrasing that maps credits to an order-level field (e.g., Availability Tier = Platinum/Gold/Silver) so the order form drives the SLOs.

— Lukas
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

--- Message 3 of 5 ---
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Reynolds <alice.reynolds@atlantichealth.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 15:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Draft addendum language + evidence checklist (for procurement)

Hi Alice,

Thanks — attached are two items: (1) a draft SLA addendum that ties an Availability Tier to a credit schedule and sample order form clause, and (2) an evidence checklist (UptimeEvidenceMatrix.xlsx) that lists artifacts we can produce during onboarding and quarterly.

Key notes on the addendum:
- We proposed three availability bands: Platinum (99.99% monthly), Gold (99.95% monthly), Silver (99.9% monthly).
- For cross-region failover, we commit to warm-standby routing with an expected switchover window of 3–7 minutes for persistent sessions; we also include an optional geo-failover annex if Atlantic needs sub-30s RTO for specific routes.
- Credit structure is tiered: partial outage (degraded serving >5% error rate sustained >30m) triggers percentage credit of monthly invoice. Full outage language remains bounded by maximum aggregate credits per month.

We left placeholders where procurement wants specific percentages — let us know the bands procurement will require and we'll populate the orderform clause and prepare redlines for your legal.

Attachments: OrderForm_Redlines.docx, UptimeEvidenceMatrix.xlsx

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Sales Operations — Redwood Inference

--- Message 4 of 5 ---
From: Tom Keller <tkeller@atlantichealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alice Reynolds <alice.reynolds@atlantichealth.com>, procurement@atlantichealth.com
Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 08:51:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft addendum language + evidence checklist (for procurement)

Thanks Marissa — useful start. A couple of clarifying asks from procurement/legal:
1) Can Redwood provide a 30/60/90 day latency histogram by route for the pilot, and commit to retaining 12 months of raw telemetry for audit?
2) For the credit schedule, procurement requests: Platinum = 99.99 (credit 20%), Gold = 99.95 (credit 10%), Silver = 99.9 (credit 5%) — is Redwood comfortable with those percentages?
3) We also need a short paragraph describing the process to request evidence during an audit and expected turnaround (we prefer <10 business days).

Also tagging legal reviewer (I can introduce once we have your redlines).

Tom Keller
Sr. Manager, Vendor Contracts
Atlantic Health Systems
Attachment: Procurement_Data_Retention_Policy.pdf

--- Message 5 of 5 ---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Keller <tkeller@atlantichealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Alice Reynolds <alice.reynolds@atlantichealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Mar 2028 11:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft addendum language + evidence checklist (for procurement)

Tom — appreciate the clear asks. Quick responses:
1) Telemetry: we will provide per-route 30/60/90 day latency histograms for the pilot and commit to 12 months of retained telemetry for audit purposes. For raw traces we require a scoped request (sampled traces are on by default; full traces can be provided under the audit process).
2) Credit percentages: Redwood is OK with the proposed bands (Platinum 20%, Gold 10%, Silver 5%) as long as the orderform caps aggregate credits to the lesser of 100% of the monthly invoice or a fixed cap we include in the addendum — we'll include the cap language in the redline.
3) Evidence request process: we propose a formal request via the provisioning portal (or a signed SOA) with a 10 business-day SLA for handoff of evidence; emergency audit requests can be prioritized and may require an NDA amendment.

Next steps: Marissa will produce a redlined order form clause that (a) maps Availability Tier to the credit schedule, (b) inserts the telemetry retention and audit flow, and (c) adds the aggregate-credit cap. Lukas — can you confirm whether we should include the optional geo-failover annex as an order-level add-on priced separately?

I'll also prepare a two-paragraph summary that procurement/legal can paste into their vendor review packet.

Thanks — Karthik
VP, Product & Reliability — Redwood Inference

--- End of thread ---
